restatements.text: Sets the title of the act.
Details findings and declarations regarding taxation, the cost of living, government spending, and transparency.
States the measure's purpose is to require audits of state programs receiving special taxes and to prohibit exemptions from the state spending limit.

Requires the California State Auditor to conduct a pre-election financial and performance audit on any program that would receive funds from a proposed special tax initiative, detailing specific topics the audit must address and requiring an executive summary in the state voter information guide.
Requires ongoing financial and performance audits every four years for programs receiving revenue from special taxes enacted on or after January 1, 2026.
Prohibits any state tax enacted or taking effect on or after January 1, 2026, from being exempted or excluded from the Government Spending Limitation.
Defines key terms used in the article, including identifying the Government Spending Limitation as Article XIII B.
Applies the new article to all statewide initiative measures submitted to voters on or after January 1, 2026.

Declares that this measure supersedes and nullifies any competing initiative on the same ballot that imposes different audit rules or exempts a tax from the Government Spending Limitation, provided this measure receives more votes.
Provides that if any part of the act is found invalid, the remaining parts stay in effect.
Sets the act to take effect immediately upon approval.
Directs that the act be liberally construed to achieve its purposes.

Requires the Attorney General to appoint independent counsel to defend the act if the Governor and Attorney General fail to do so, and establishes a continuous appropriation to cover those legal costs.

evidence.quote: No state tax that is enacted or takes effect on or after January 1, 2026 shall be exempted or excluded from the Government Spending Limitation.
evidence.why: It prevents the state from spending special tax revenue outside of established constitutional spending limits.

evidence.quote: the California State Auditor shall commence with the preparation of a pre-election financial and performance audit of each of the program(s) that would receive moneys from the special tax.
evidence.why: It creates a new mandate and expands the auditing duties of the California State Auditor.

evidence.quote: the California State Auditor shall commence with the preparation of a pre-election financial and performance audit of each of the program(s) that would receive moneys from the special tax.
evidence.why: Requires an upfront public audit of programs slated to receive special tax revenues.

evidence.quote: the California State Auditor shall conduct ongoing financial and performance audits of each program that receives moneys from the special tax.
evidence.why: Requires ongoing reviews of how special tax revenues are spent.

evidence.quote: a continuous appropriation is hereby made from the General Fund to the Controller, without regard to fiscal years, in an amount necessary to cover the costs of retaining independent counsel
evidence.why: Creates an automatic, continuously available stream of funding to pay for independent counsel to defend the act.

evidence.quote: No state tax that is enacted or takes effect on or after January 1, 2026 shall be exempted or excluded from the Government Spending Limitation.
evidence.why: Locks in the existing Government Spending Limitation, removing the flexibility to exempt future taxes from the cap.

evidence.quote: No state tax that is enacted or takes effect on or after January 1, 2026 shall be exempted or excluded from the Government Spending Limitation.
evidence.why: Restricts what voters can enact via initiative by banning measures from bypassing the spending limit.

evidence.quote: In the event that this initiative measure appears on the same statewide election ballot as another initiative measure that (A) imposes different audit rules on special taxes; or (B) contains a state tax that is exempted or excluded from the Government Spending Limitation, then that other initiative measure shall be deemed to be in conflict with this measure. In the event that this initiative measure receives a greater number of affirmative votes, the provisions of this measure shall prevail in their entirety, and all the provisions of the other measure shall be null and void.
evidence.why: Explicitly voids competing citizen initiatives on the same ballot if they contain conflicting tax or audit rules.

evidence.quote: The State of California shall not impose, collect, or enforce any state tax that is enacted or takes effect on or after January 1, 2026 if the state tax is exempted or excluded from the Government Spending Limitation.
evidence.why: Prevents the state from collecting newly enacted taxes if they attempt to bypass the statutory spending cap, thereby limiting the total funding available.

evidence.quote: the California State Auditor shall commence with the preparation of a pre-election financial and performance audit of each of the program(s) that would receive moneys from the special tax.
evidence.why: It expands the state's auditing programs by mandating new pre-election audits.

evidence.quote: No state tax that is enacted or takes effect on or after January 1, 2026 shall be exempted or excluded from the Government Spending Limitation.
evidence.why: It restricts government spending authority by tying all new special taxes to a strict spending cap.

analysis.answer: Current law was not provided. The measure introduces a new requirement that the California State Auditor prepare financial and performance audits of state programs slated to receive funds from any proposed special tax initiative.

The California State Auditor will incur direct costs to conduct these pre-election audits quickly enough to meet voter guide deadlines. While the measure directs reimbursement from the special tax revenue if the initiative passes, these costs are unrecouped if the measure fails or before the tax begins generating revenue. There is also an opportunity cost, as auditor staff may need to be diverted from other investigations.

The text asserts a problem of taxes being passed that bypass the state's spending limit, causing spending to spiral out of control. The mechanism addresses this by strictly prohibiting any new tax enacted after January 1, 2026, from being exempted from the Government Spending Limitation.

The California State Auditor gains significant discretion and power, as their detailed assessments of a program's efficiency and waste—including mandatory recommendations for 10% cost savings—will be directly placed in the state voter information guide, potentially shaping the electorate's view of special tax initiatives.

The broader economic effect of imposing strict spending limits (like the Gann Limit) on public services is disputed. Some research suggests such limits improve government efficiency and safeguard taxpayers from burdensome costs, while other findings indicate they artificially constrain needed investments in infrastructure and public services during times of economic growth.

The continuous appropriation from the General Fund guarantees that direct costs for hiring independent counsel will be fully covered if the Governor and Attorney General refuse to defend the measure, creating a budgetary expense outside the standard annual appropriations process.

flags.quote: The provisions of this Act are severable.
This Act shall take effect at the earliest possible date in accordance with Section 10 of Article II of the California Constitution. This Act shall become operative on the same day it takes effect.
flags.note: Immediate effective date upon voter approval.

flags.quote: Notwithstanding anything to the contrary contained in Chapter 6 (commencing with Section 12500) of Part 2 of Division 3 of Title 2 of the Government Code or any other law
flags.note: Override language used to mandate the appointment of independent counsel despite existing statutes granting the Attorney General sole defense authority.
